newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen opening strong, Intel news cited.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen opening strong, Intel news cited.

text.p: Wall Street stocks should open higher on Tuesday after yesterday's record close, lifted higher by good news for Intel Corp, Philip Morris Cos Inc and Ford Motor Co.

"We could see a gap opening on the upside," said Peter Cardillo, director of research for Westfalia Investments, citing strength in the technology, consumer goods and auto sectors after the positive news.

Microprocessor giant Intel said after the market close Monday it expects third quarter revenues to come in higher then expected, beating second-quarter revenues of $4.62 billion. The stock soared in after-hours trading.

"While the market looked tired in the final hours yesterday, the Intel news could revive the tech sector. It should be helpful for the whole industry, and lead to a firmer opening," said Prudential market analysts Larry Wachtel.

News that Ford reached a tentative contract with the United Auto Workers and that a Florida court threw out the bulk of claims in a Medicaid suit brought by that state against the tobacco industry should also boost stocks.
Philip Morris shares rose to 94-1/2 in London from its New York close of 92 overnight.

Cardillo said, "Consumer stocks should get a boost from that news, Intel will boost tech stocks, and Ford will boost the auto stocks. If industrial production comes in line, it won't affect the bond market. Unless bonds fall apart, we could close in new record territory again. The bull is alive."
At 0915/1315, August industrial production and capacity utilization figures are due. Industrial production is forecast to rise 0.4 percent compared to a rise of 0.1 percent in July.
Capacity utilization is inch higher to 83.3 percent, compared to 83.2 percent in July.
The long bond was off one tick to yield 6.95 percent.
Standard & Poor's December futures rose 1.5 to 692.25.
Tokyo stocks galloped higher, with the benchmark Nikkei 225 up over two percent to close 468 points higher at 21,311.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 4.2 to 3973. U.S. stocks in London was mostly firmer in active trading.

Movie theater companies planning gargantuan size theatre complexes with thirty screens, like AMC Entertainment Inc, Cineplex Odeon Corp and Regal Cinemas Inc may not have enough good movies to fill up the seats, according to the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column.

America Online's move from the Nasdaq to the New York Stock Exchange yesterday also comes with a new marketing strategy to keep more subscribers and boost growth faster, the New York Times Marketplace column said.
